summary:
NEDA RotaNA is a digital decision-support platform for agriculture, specifically designed for Yen Thanh District (Nghe An Province) – a major rice-growing hub with over 26,500 hectares of cultivated land. We integrated multi-satellite data from NASA spanning 9 years (including soil moisture from SMAP, precipitation from GPM, 30m resolution NDVI biomass indices from Landsat, and agricultural climate data from NASA POWER) combined with an Ensemble Random Forest machine learning model, achieving an accuracy of 85.1%.

The system addresses three severe climate challenges: early warning for spring frosts damaging young seedlings; mitigating Foehn winds (hot and dry winds >= 35°C) during the rice heading stage; and minimizing harvest-season flood risks along the Vach Bac canal. Additionally, remote sensing technology supports monitoring post-season soil fallow periods, helping to eliminate 85–90% of rice blast fungus spores and restore soil fertility.

This project plays a pivotal role in transitioning from experience-based farming to space-empowered precision agriculture, thereby protecting over 180,000 tons of rice annually while offering high scalability across the North Central region of Vietnam.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS: NEDA RotaNA – YEN THANH RICE SEASON EVALUATION & YIELD FORECASTING SYSTEM 2027

1. What does this project do and how does it work? NEDA RotaNA is a Digital Cockpit platform applying NASA multi-satellite remote sensing technology and Artificial Intelligence (Random Forest Machine Learning) to serve crop season management and rice yield forecasting for Yen Thanh District (Nghe An Province) – the largest high-quality pure rice granary in North Central Vietnam with a cultivated area of over 26,500 ha.

The system operates on a closed-loop 3-tier workflow:

  • Data Acquisition & Integration Tier: Synchronizes a continuous 9-year time series (2018–2026) from 4 NASA satellite sources:
    • NASA SMAP: Measures root-zone (0–100 cm) and surface soil moisture using L-band microwaves on a 2–3 day cycle for early drought warning.
    • NASA GPM IMERG: Estimates global accumulated rainfall and extreme storm/flood frequency.
    • Landsat 8/9 (30m) & MODIS: Provides vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI, LAI) and Land Surface Temperature (LST).
    • NASA POWER: Provides over 3,200 consecutive days of solar radiation, maximum/minimum temperatures, and Southwest Foehn wind days (>= 35°C).
    • Data is standardized with Yen Thanh field-measured soil data (pH 5.62, 26.9% clay content) and a Digital Elevation Model (DEM).
    • Cultivation Suitability Score Model: S = 100 - (P_temp + P_drought + P_flood) quantifies real-time disaster risks, classifying into 3 decisions: Recommended for Sowing (S >= 80), Conditional Sowing (50 <= S < 80), and Postpone Sowing (S < 50).
    • Ensemble Random Forest Machine Learning Model (100 decision trees): Forecasts 2027 rice yield for the Winter-Spring and Summer-Autumn crops with a validation accuracy of R2 = 85.1% (MAE = ±0.51 quintals/ha).
    • Random Forest Classifier Model: Automatically classifies 4 field agronomic growth phases with 88.8% accuracy.
  • Visualization & Decision Support Tier: Folium digital map integrating Landsat 30m / Google Satellite optical imagery layers, real-time monitoring of 4 key digitalized commune clusters, and a free-form climate scenario simulator (What-If Simulation).

2. What benefits does the project bring?

  • For local authorities and agricultural management agencies: Provides objective scientific evidence to issue accurate seasonal calendars, eliminating the risks of intuition-based planting; supports optimal water release/closure regulation for the Ba Ra Do Luong major irrigation system and operation of the Kenh Vach Bac flood drainage system.
  • For local farmers: Provides 7–15 days early disaster warnings (early Winter-Spring severe cold spells, Foehn wind heat shocks scorching pollen during heading, and harvest-season flooding); fully protects grain yield and minimizes fertilizer and pesticide costs through natural soil-restoring winter fallow plowing.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Economic Impact: Firmly protects food production of over 180,000 tons of paddy per year for Yen Thanh District (contributing ~15% of Nghe An Province's total rice output); optimizes average yield to reach 64–70 quintals/ha, increasing income for tens of thousands of farming households.
  • Environmental & Social Impact: Promotes sustainable circular agriculture: by using remote sensing to monitor bare land and trigger 18–22 cm deep fallow plowing during 30–45 dry winter days, it eliminates 85–90% of rice blast fungus pathogens and reduces dependence on agrochemicals.
  • Scalability Potential: The platform features an open modular architecture, ready to scale to neighboring districts (Dien Chau, Do Luong, Nghi Loc) and all irrigated rice plains across North Central Vietnam.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, and software were used?

  • Programming Language: Python 3.12 (core language for data processing, spatial analysis, and AI models).
  • Data Science & Machine Learning: scikit-learn (training RandomForestRegressor, RandomForestClassifier, hyperparameter tuning), numpy, pandas, scipy.
  • Application Interface & Visualization: streamlit (building the real-time interactive web application), plotly (ecological spline charts, waterfall charts, correlation matrices), folium & streamlit-folium (interactive GIS geospatial maps).
  • Remote Sensing & GIS Processing: Google Earth Engine (GEE), geopandas, shapely, GeoJSON.
  • Official NASA Satellite Data Sources: NASA Earthdata, NASA SMAP L-Band L4, NASA GPM IMERG, Landsat 8/9 OLI/TIRS (USGS), MODIS Terra/Aqua, NASA POWER API.
  • Development & Testing Environment: Windows 11, PowerShell, Git, unittest (built a suite of 9 automated unit tests verifying 100% system integrity).

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

  • Tightly linking Space Remote Sensing with Local Agronomic Knowledge: The project goes beyond passive satellite observation by turning optical indices into specific production directives for each pure rice variety (ST25, J02, TBR225, Khang Dan 18) across commune clusters.
  • Discovering and Digitalizing the "Art of Winter Fallow Plowing": Uses the Landsat remote sensing threshold NDVI < 0.40 to detect bare soil and trigger deep crack-plowing for soil fertility restoration – elevating a traditional farming practice with satellite science.
  • Random Forest Machine Learning decoding "Feature Importance": Completely overcomes complex climate non-linearity (moderate temperature is beneficial, whereas >= 35°C scorches panicles); quantifies for the first time the contribution weight of each satellite variable to grain yield (Solar Radiation 48.2%, SMAP 18.8%, NDVI 15.3%, Foehn Wind 8.5%).
  • Live Scenario Simulator (What-If Simulation Sandbox): Allows users to directly drag sliders to test climate change scenarios and receive instant yield responses within 0.1 seconds.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Ecological Factors & Agronomic Laws: Sensitive tolerance thresholds of rice at each growth stage: seedling cold-death threshold (Tmin < 15°C), Foehn wind pollen-scorching threshold (Tmax >= 35–37°C with RH < 55%), and harvest-season flooding threshold (> 350 mm).
  • Hydrological & Basin Topography Factors: Low-lying basin topography receiving floodwaters from Kenh Vach Bac and 85–90% reliance on gravity-fed irrigation from the Ba Ra Do Luong hydraulic works.
  • Field Soil Factors: Organic matter content (19.6 g/kg), soil acidity (pH 5.62), clay content (26.9%), and sand content (44.3%) extracted from empirical field data in Yen Thanh.
  • User Experience (UX/UI): User-friendly interface design utilizing international traffic-light color visualization (Green - Yellow - Red) so both agricultural officials and local farmers can easily understand and operate the system immediately.
